*(executable, owned by root, placed on the target host)*  

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Atomic deploy for /srv/myapp
#   - unpacks a new release under /srv/myapp/releases/<timestamp>
#   - swaps the /srv/myapp/current symlink atomically
#   - runs a health check against http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz
#   - rolls back automatically on failure
#   - logs every step to /srv/myapp/deploy.log
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

set -euo pipefail

# ---------- configuration ----------
APP_ROOT="/srv/myapp"
RELEASES_DIR="${APP_ROOT}/releases"
CURRENT_LINK="${APP_ROOT}/current"
LOG_FILE="${APP_ROOT}/deploy.log"
HEALTH_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz"
# -----------------------------------

# Helper: write a timestamped line to the log and also to stdout
log() {
    local msg="$*"
    local ts
    ts="$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
    printf '[%s] %s\n' "$ts" "$msg" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Sanity checks
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
log "=== STARTING DEPLOY for $(basename "$APP_ROOT") ==="

# Ensure the current symlink exists and points to a valid release
if [[ ! -L "$CURRENT_LINK" ]]; then
    log "ERROR: current symlink $CURRENT_LINK is missing or not a symlink – aborting."
    exit 1
fi
if [[ ! -d "$(readlink -f "$CURRENT_LINK")" ]]; then
    log "ERROR: current symlink target does not exist – aborting."
    exit 1
fi

# Verify we have a release tarball (or whatever you use) in /tmp or similar
# This is just an example – adapt to your source of the new release.
NEW_RELEASE_TAR="${APP_ROOT}/../new_release.tar.gz"
if [[ ! -f "$NEW_RELEASE_TAR" ]]; then
    log "ERROR: release archive $NEW_RELEASE_TAR not found – aborting."
    exit 1
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Unpack the new release into a timestamped directory
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
TIMESTAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
NEW_RELEASE_DIR="${RELEASES_DIR}/${TIMESTAMP}"
log "Creating new release directory ${NEW_RELEASE_DIR}"
mkdir -p "$NEW_RELEASE_DIR"

# Extract – you may replace this with your own deployment method (e.g. rsync)
log "Extracting release archive"
tar -xzf "$NEW_RELEASE_TAR" -C "$NEW_RELEASE_DIR"

# Verify that the release looks sane (optional but cheap)
if [[ ! -f "${NEW_RELEASE_DIR}/bin/start.sh" ]]; then
    log "ERROR: release directory missing expected start script – aborting."
    rm -rf "$NEW_RELEASE_DIR"
    exit 1
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Switch the symlink atomically
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Keep a reference to the previous target for rollback
PREV_TARGET="$(readlink -f "$CURRENT_LINK")"

log "Switching symlink $CURRENT_LINK -> ${NEW_RELEASE_DIR}"
# Use mv to rename the old symlink out of the way (kept for rollback)
mv "$CURRENT_LINK" "${CURRENT_LINK}.old_$(date +%s)" || {
    log "ERROR: could not rename old symlink – aborting."
    exit 1
}
ln -sfn "$NEW_RELEASE_DIR" "$CURRENT_LINK"

log "Symlink now points to ${NEW_RELEASE_DIR}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Run health check – do NOT delete old release yet
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Running health check against $HEALTH_URL"
if ! curl -fsS "$HEALTH_URL" >/dev/null; then
    log "ERROR: health check failed – rolling back."

    # Restore previous symlink
    log "Restoring previous symlink target ${PREV_TARGET}"
    ln -sfn "$PREV_TARGET" "$CURRENT_LINK"
    log "Rollback complete."

    # Optionally keep the failed release for debugging
    log "Keeping failed release at ${NEW_RELEASE_DIR} for inspection."

    log "=== DEPLOY FAILED ==="
    exit 1
fi

log "Health check succeeded."

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Cleanup – remove the previous release (the one we renamed)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ -e "${CURRENT_LINK}.old_$(date +%s)" ]]; then
    # The old symlink file name is unique because we added a timestamp.
    # Find it safely:
    OLD_LINK=$(find "$(dirname "$CURRENT_LINK")" -maxdepth 1 -name "$(basename "$CURRENT_LINK").old_*" -print -quit)
    if [[ -n "$OLD_LINK" ]]; then
        log "Removing old release directory ${OLD_LINK}"
        rm -rf "${OLD_LINK}"
    fi
fi

log "=== DEPLOY SUCCESSFUL ==="
exit 0
```
